recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片充滿中型芽細胞，核圓至卵圓、部分有凹痕，染色質細緻、核仁不明顯，只有一圈淡藍色無顆粒細胞質，為典型淋巴芽細胞樣外觀；T 系需流式確認。
features: Medium-sized blasts, roughly 1.5–2 times RBC diameter
High N:C ratio with thin rim of agranular pale blue cytoplasm
Round to oval nuclei, some indented or notched
Finely granular chromatin with inconspicuous nucleoli
No Auer rods, granules or significant vacuolation
Normal maturing hematopoietic cells not evident
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a hypercellular field replaced by sheets of medium-sized blasts. The blasts have high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, round to oval nuclei with occasional indentations, finely granular chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and scant agranular pale blue cytoplasm. No Auer rods or cytoplasmic granules are identified, and maturing myeloid and erythroid elements are not seen in this field. The morphology is lymphoblastic; T-lineage requires immunophenotypic confirmation (cytoplasmic CD3, TdT). Findings are consistent with T-lymphoblastic leukemia.

ddx.vs: Morphologically identical; distinguished by B-cell antigen expression (CD19, CD79a, PAX5) and absence of cytoplasmic CD3.
Myeloblasts often show more open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, occasional granules or Auer rods, and MPO positivity (≥3% blasts).
Burkitt cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm with prominent lipid vacuoles and a mature sIg+ TdT-negative phenotype.
